hypotheses.statement: Value-only compare-exchange is insufficient as the semantic identity test for versioned Clay/UnifiedDB/Frank state because an A->B->A transition can make a stale observer's expected value equal again while the state identity has changed.
evidence: Rust std atomic compare_exchange ABA warning
hypotheses.falsifier: Demonstrate a value-only CAS contract that rejects all stale A->...->A transitions without adding version/identity information or a stronger external serialization invariant.

hypotheses.statement: For Clay semantic state where equality is not identity, compare-exchange should bind an explicit version/epoch/identity token in addition to the value; raw value-only CAS may remain available only for types/resources whose contract proves equality is sufficient identity.
evidence: RAE latest stack semantic epoch rules
hypotheses.falsifier: Find a required Clay workload where version binding changes correct semantics or cannot be lowered while an independently safe non-versioned identity contract exists.

hypotheses.statement: Weak-CAS retry/spurious-failure count belongs to execution trace identity, not semantic operation identity; one stable semantic CAS intent/outcome may have multiple physical attempt traces.
hypotheses.falsifier: Produce a Clay program whose intended semantic result necessarily depends on the number of weak-CAS physical retries rather than on an explicit observable retry-budget/timing construct.

hypotheses.statement: For BASE, SeqCst is the safest portable default atomic ordering while weaker Relaxed/Acquire/Release/AcqRel orderings should remain explicit typed opt-ins rather than host-default behavior.
hypotheses.falsifier: Show that a weaker fixed default preserves all accepted ClayCode application and FRANK semantics across target backends with a materially better measured cost and no additional repair/verification burden.

hypotheses.statement: The ClayCode type/effect checker should validate success and failure memory-order combinations rather than passing arbitrary host orderings through FFI; failure-order semantics are load-only and must reject release-style orderings where the target model forbids them.
hypotheses.falsifier: A backend-neutral lowering proof shows arbitrary order pairs can be normalized safely without source-visible or IR-visible validation.

counterhypotheses.statement: Raw value-only CAS is sufficient for all Clay state because atomicity already prevents stale writes.
counterhypotheses.result: The deterministic ABA experiment produced stale success in 200000/200000 constructed A->...->A cases.

counterhypotheses.statement: Every weak-CAS retry should be part of the semantic hash/event sequence.
counterhypotheses.result: 100000 identical semantic operations produced one semantic hash but 16 valid physical retry-trace hashes; C11 and Node reached the same exact result with different retry counts.

counterhypotheses.statement: ClayCode should expose only SeqCst atomics permanently.
counterhypotheses.reason: Safe first-release simplification is plausible, but target-specific performance/algorithm requirements have not been measured deeply enough to forbid weaker explicit orderings forever.

counterhypotheses.statement: ClayCode can leave memory ordering entirely to the host backend as an implementation detail.
counterhypotheses.reason: Current primary specifications expose materially different ordering contracts, so silent host inheritance would make cross-backend semantics under-specified.

language_change_rule: No surface-syntax change is proposed. First express the candidate in canonical IR/runtime metadata and require executable lowering counterexamples before changing the language surface.
